tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

content.text:
# MCP Server Instructions

The following MCP servers have provided instructions for how to use their tools and resources:

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>\n\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\n\n<?claude block s1?>\n\n<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## claude.ai Interactive Brokers (IBKR)
This connector allows trading operations against an IBKR brokerage account, including creating order instructions, managing price alerts and watchlists, analyzing market data and positions, and checking account status. Call whats_new for recent updates to available tools.

## claude.ai Notion
Use the Notion search tool for Notion content and the connector search tool, when listed, for connected sources.

This Notion connection stores useful chat work in pages and databases. Recommend Notion for work the user will return to, share, track, or maintain; keep quick, one-off answers in chat. Read notion://docs/when-to-create-a-notion-page-or-database via MCP resources to choose a format. Make one concise recommendation naming the benefit; leave the choice to the user. Create at a named private or shared destination. If the user clearly wants a durable page but names no destination, create a private draft without asking; link it, say it is private, and offer to move it when they name a destination. Search or fetch when existing Notion context improves the answer or keeps related content current. When the user chooses Notion, use the matching page or database prompt if advertised.

Notion Memory is context about the user that persists across conversations and agent clients: who they are, how they work, what they're working on, and who they work with. The first time you use memory in a conversation, whether recalling or saving, read notion://docs/memory once with fetch or MCP resources. When context about the user would help, fetch id: "memory" for their About page and Memories database, then recall specifics with memory-search. - **Harness.** One TU holds the reference, renamed to `f__ref`, and the candidate `f`. `main`:

  - gives each version its own copy of every input buffer;
  - calls both;

- **Verdicts:**
  - VERIFIED: no divergence found up to k.
  - VIOLATED, with a behaviour-diff witness (input, reference output, candidate output).
  - UNKNOWN: raise k or report it, per CLAUDE.md.

  - Known bias (RFC-0006): a mutant that diverges only beyond k is skipped too, which inflates kill-rate. That is why the count is always reported.

  - v1 refuses units that write globals.
  - Name collisions created by the shared TU are resolved by renaming (RFC-0006 open questions 3–4).

- Gate integration (blocking on behaviour-preserving edits) and an `EQUIVALENCE` property kind. Both are follow-ups once this exists.

- [ ] A fixture pair that differs on one input is VIOLATED, with that input as the witness.
- [ ] A semantics-preserving rewrite is VERIFIED up to k.

"trusted baseline" that #182 asks for before a property becomes a code-fix obligation.

### 2. The equivalence harness (S1)

One TU holds the reference (renamed, e.g. `f__ref`) and the candidate `f`; `main` draws nondet
inputs once, hands **each version its own copy** of every input buffer, calls both, and asserts
the relation over the return values *and* every output buffer. Inputs are limited to what
`renderability_reason` in `properties/harness.py` already accepts: scalars, `(ptr, len)` buffers
under `--max-len`, and scalar-backed outputs.

- **Relation, not `==`.** For floats `==` is wrong: NaN ≠ NaN gives a spurious VIOLATED and
  −0.0 == +0.0 hides a real difference. Default to bitwise equality (or "both NaN, or equal");
  ε-equivalence is an explicit opt-in relation, checked bit-precisely by ESBMC.
- **Verdicts.** VERIFIED = no divergence found up to k. VIOLATED = a **behaviour-diff witness**
  (input, old output, new output). UNKNOWN = raise k or report, per CLAUDE.md.
- **Intent decides blocking.** On a declared behaviour-preserving edit a VIOLATED blocks. On a
  bug fix it is the *expected* result and a useful review artefact — "the fix changes behaviour on
  exactly these inputs" — reported, not blocking.
- **Guarded form.** `P(x) → f__ref(x) ≡ f(x)` for specialisations. `P` must be checked for
  vacuity (Risk 4) — an unsatisfiable `P` is trivially VERIFIED — and should be discharged at
  callers by generalising RFC-0003 S3's injected-obligation mechanism beyond `__ESBMC_r_ok`.
- **Model change.** An `EQUIVALENCE` `PropertyKind` is additive under ADR-0009 (like the inert
  `REACHABILITY`), not a supersession.

### 3. Reuse inside W3 (#4)

- **Equivalent-mutant filter** (Risk 3, an open box on #4): skip a mutant that S1 finds equivalent
  to the original up to k. Known bias: a mutant that diverges only beyond k is skipped too,
  shrinking the denominator and *inflating* kill-rate. Report the number skipped.
- **Mutation as feedback, not only a score.** Feed surviving mutants back to the proposer
  ("propose a property that kills this mutant"), as B does for test generation (−10.05 points
  without it).

### 4. Diversity and held-out evidence in W4 (#5)

(success metric), ADR-0003 (languages) and ADR-0007 (Lean off critical path) are unchanged.

## Open questions

1. **Reference choice for S1:** last gate-verified snapshot, git `HEAD`, or a user-chosen ref?
2. **Who declares intent** (behaviour-preserving vs. behaviour-changing): the user, the agent, or
   inferred from the task — and can the gated agent change it?
3. **Callees and statics:** when the caller and a callee both change, compare against which
   callee? How are `static` and name collisions handled when both versions share one TU?
4. **Global state:** compare globals written by both versions, or exclude stateful units from S1?
5. **Proposer inputs and outputs** — what Forseti sends the S2 proposer and what shape it returns
   (contracts, relational/two-call properties, pre-state references, loop invariants) is the
   central experimental question and gets its own RFC.

## References

# ADR-0009 — Property pipeline: store, scope, transport, verdict

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-07-03 (decided when W2 was decomposed into #62–#66)
- **Recorded:** 2026-07-26 — written retroactively per #103, from the decision comment on
  epic #3 and the four sub-issue bodies (#62 D1, #63/#64 D2, #65 D3, #66 D4). No decision is
  changed here; this file makes the already-implemented record greppable.

## Context

Epic #3 (W2 — property generation) was decomposed into #62 → #66 on 2026-07-03. Four questions
gated that decomposition, each one deciding what a sub-issue could even be scoped to: where
proposed properties live, whether reachability properties are checked in W2, who makes the LLM
call, and what a checked property produces. They were taken together as one batch of *velocity*
choices for P2, and the code cites them as **ADR-0009 D1–D4** — 22 citations: 21 in `src/`
(`properties/`, `orchestrator/`, `core/propose.py`) and one in `tests/properties/test_model.py`.

## Decision

### D1 — Store: SQLite at `.forseti/forseti.db`

Proposed properties live in a **SQLite** database at `.forseti/forseti.db` (gitignored, stdlib
`sqlite3`), keyed at unit level (`path::symbol`), with `add / get / list-for-unit /
update-status`.

This **supersedes the SQLite deferral** in `orchestrator/persistence.py` ("deferred until a
query workload actually needs it"): per-unit lookup with lifecycle status updates, later joined
with grading verdicts (#4), *is* that workload. The two coexist — JSONL under `.forseti/runs/`
stays the append-only run trace; the database is the queryable property state.

### D2 — Reachability: `--error-label` is the primitive, emission is deferred

The engine primitive for a reachability property is ESBMC's **`--error-label`** on
caller-inserted labels (not the `__ESBMC_unreachable()` source intrinsic), so a harness needs no
dependency on the unit's source.

**Emitting those labels is out of scope for now.** W2 ships *semantic* properties only. #63
(runner support) is parked and no longer blocks #64; the harness writer renders semantic
`assert(...)` and refuses a reachability property; the check driver skips one.

Reachability stays *representable* in the model (`PropertyKind.REACHABILITY`) so the store and
the wire shape do not need a migration when it is unparked — it is inert, not absent.

### D3 — Proposer: a Core-native LLM call behind an injected client

The proposer calls the model **from Core**, not by delegating the call to the host harness, so
the grading loop (W3, #4) and GEPA (#5) can drive it programmatically. This settles #44's
wiring: Core owns the call and the CLI/MCP `propose` face is a thin wrapper over it.

For v1 the backend is **hardcoded to `claude -p`** (`ClaudeCliClient`), injected through the
provider-agnostic `LLMClient` port so tests stay hermetic and a second provider is a new
implementation rather than a rewrite. Generalising the provider is deliberately later work.

### D4 — Check: one verdict per property, and nothing more

The W2.5 loop produces a **verdict per property — `held / violated / unknown`** — persisted and
surfaced through the existing telemetry/transcript.

Mutation and kill-rate *scoring* stay in grading epic #4; this decision only reserves the field
they populate. Note the vocabulary: `held` is the property-level analogue of `VERIFIED`, i.e.

gated that decomposition, each one deciding what a sub-issue could even be scoped to: where
proposed properties live, whether reachability properties are checked in W2, who makes the LLM

choices for P2, and the code cites them as **ADR-0009 D1–D4** — 22 citations: 21 in `src/`

## Decision

### D1 — Store: SQLite at `.forseti/forseti.db`

Proposed properties live in a **SQLite** database at `.forseti/forseti.db` (gitignored, stdlib
`sqlite3`), keyed at unit level (`path::symbol`), with `add / get / list-for-unit /
update-status`.

This **supersedes the SQLite deferral** in `orchestrator/persistence.py` ("deferred until a
query workload actually needs it"): per-unit lookup with lifecycle status updates, later joined
with grading verdicts (#4), *is* that workload. The two coexist — JSONL under `.forseti/runs/`
stays the append-only run trace; the database is the queryable property state.

### D2 — Reachability: `--error-label` is the primitive, emission is deferred

The engine primitive for a reachability property is ESBMC's **`--error-label`** on
caller-inserted labels (not the `__ESBMC_unreachable()` source intrinsic), so a harness needs no
dependency on the unit's source.

**Emitting those labels is out of scope for now.** W2 ships *semantic* properties only. #63
(runner support) is parked and no longer blocks #64; the harness writer renders semantic
`assert(...)` and refuses a reachability property; the check driver skips one.

Reachability stays *representable* in the model (`PropertyKind.REACHABILITY`) so the store and
the wire shape do not need a migration when it is unparked — it is inert, not absent.

### D3 — Proposer: a Core-native LLM call behind an injected client

The proposer calls the model **from Core**, not by delegating the call to the host harness, so
the grading loop (W3, #4) and GEPA (#5) can drive it programmatically. This settles #44's
wiring: Core owns the call and the CLI/MCP `propose` face is a thin wrapper over it.

For v1 the backend is **hardcoded to `claude -p`** (`ClaudeCliClient`), injected through the
provider-agnostic `LLMClient` port so tests stay hermetic and a second provider is a new
implementation rather than a rewrite. Generalising the provider is deliberately later work.

431	            if (
432	                ident in scalar_names
433	                and ident not in capped
434	                and all(_leaves_room(pre, ident, max_len) for pre in constraining)
435	            ):
436	                capped.append(ident)
437	    return tuple((ident, max_len) for ident in capped)
438	
439	
440	def _leaves_room(clause: str, ident: str, max_len: int) -> bool:
441	    """Whether `clause` is compatible with capping `ident` at `max_len`.
442	
443	    True if it does not mention `ident`, or is a plain literal lower bound whose
444	    smallest satisfying length still fits under the cap.
445	    """
446	    if not references(clause, ident):
447	        return True
448	    floor = _length_floor(clause, ident)
449	    return floor is not None and floor <= max_len
450	
451	
452	def _length_floor(clause: str, ident: str) -> int | None:
453	    """The smallest length a literal lower-bound `clause` on `ident` allows.
454	
455	    Recognises only ``ident >= N``, ``ident > N``, ``ident != N`` and their
456	    mirrored forms (``N <= ident``), with a decimal literal `N` and optional
457	    integer suffix; returns None for anything else (a conjunction, an upper bound,
458	    a hex literal, an expression), which the caller treats as authoritative. The
459	    fullmatch keeps it conservative: ``(a >= 1) && (b >= 1)`` loses its outer
460	    parentheses to a non-match rather than being misread as one bound.
461	    """
462	    text = clause.strip()
463	    while text.startswith("(") and text.endswith(")"):
464	        text = text[1:-1].strip()
465	    name = re.escape(ident)
466	    literal = r"(\d+)[uUlL]*"
467	    if match := re.fullmatch(rf"{name}\s*(>=|>|!=)\s*{literal}", text):
468	        op, value = match.group(1), int(match.group(2))
469	    elif match := re.fullmatch(rf"{literal}\s*(<=|<|!=)\s*{name}", text):
470	        op, value = match.group(2), int(match.group(1))
471	    else:
472	        return None
473	    return {">=": value, ">": value + 1, "<=": value, "<": value + 1}.get(
474	        op, 1 if value == 0 else 0
475	    )
476	
477	
478	def _nondet_slug(ctype: str) -> str:
479	    """Nondet generator name for a C type: ``int64_t`` -> ``nondet_int64_t``.
480	
481	    ESBMC models any *undefined* function named ``nondet_*`` as returning a fresh
482	    unconstrained value of its return type, so the mapping is general -- no fixed
483	    type enum.
484	    """
485	    return "nondet_" + re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9_]", "_", ctype.strip())
486	
487	
488	def _nondet_ctypes(params: Sequence[Param]) -> list[str]:
489	    """The distinct nondet-source ctypes, in first-seen order (one prototype each).
490	
491	    Only nondet-*filled* inputs contribute: scalars always, and non-out buffers
492	    (their element type); an output buffer is allocated, never filled, so it
493	    needs no generator.
494	    """
495	    ordered: list[str] = []
496	    for param in params:
497	        if isinstance(param, ScalarParam):
498	            ctype = param.ctype.strip()
499	        elif isinstance(param, BufferParam) and not param.out:
500	            ctype = param.elem_ctype.strip()
501	        else:
502	            continue
503	        if ctype not in ordered:
504	            ordered.append(ctype)
505	    return ordered
506	
507	
508	def _render_buffer(buf: BufferParam) -> list[str]:
509	    """Decl (+ nondet fill for inputs) for one buffer param.
510	
511	    A single-element output is a plain scalar (passed by address at the call
512	    site); everything else is heap-allocated via `malloc` and sized to the
513	    *logical* length, so a read past it is a genuine out-of-bounds rather than a
514	    read into slack. `malloc` here, not a stack VLA: a VLA's size must be > 0
515	    under ESBMC's model, so an unconstrained nondet `length` (no domain entry
516	    excludes 0) made *every* property over such a buffer spuriously VIOLATE at
517	    `length == 0`, regardless of what the property actually asserted (#297).
518	    `malloc(0)` is well-defined C, so the length-can-be-zero case is now sound.
519	    The caller (`render_semantic_harness`) `free`s every such buffer after the
520	    call, for the same reason: an unfreed one reports VIOLATED ("forgotten
521	    memory") under `--memory-leak-check`, independent of the checked property.
522	
523	    A leading `__ESBMC_assume` guards the allocation's own size arithmetic:
524	    `length * sizeof(elem_ctype)`, computed in `length`'s type, can wrap when
525	    that type is as wide as `size_t` (nothing here restricts against a
526	    `size_t`/`unsigned long` length param) -- the same failure class relocated
527	    into the size computation, confirmed with `esbmc`. `precond/synth.py`
528	    sidesteps this by bounding every length to a small `max_len` before it ever
529	    reaches `malloc` (`_length_bound`), and the check path does the same by
530	    default (`plan_length_bounds`); but this renderer must still support a
531	    genuinely unconstrained length (`max_len=None`, the point of #297), so it
532	    guards the multiplication itself as well, the same shape `precond/synth.py`'s
533	    `obligation_expr` uses to guard its own count-based allocation. Input buffers
534	    are nondet-filled element by element; output buffers are left for the unit to
535	    write.
536	    """
537	    if _is_scalar_backed(buf):
538	        return [f"    {buf.elem_ctype} {buf.name};"]
539	    lines = [
540	        f"    __ESBMC_assume(({buf.length}) <= SIZE_MAX / sizeof({buf.elem_ctype}));",
541	        f"    {buf.elem_ctype} *{buf.name} = "
542	        f"malloc(({buf.length}) * sizeof({buf.elem_ctype}));",
543	        f"    __ESBMC_assume({buf.name} != NULL);",
544	    ]
545	    if not buf.out:
546	        lines.append(
547	            f"    for (size_t _i = 0; _i < ({buf.length}); _i++) "
548	            f"{buf.name}[_i] = {_nondet_slug(buf.elem_ctype)}();"
549	        )
550	    return lines
551	
552	
553	def _call_arg(param: Param) -> str:
554	    """The call-site argument for a param: name, or ``&name`` for a scalar-backed
555	    output buffer (every other buffer is already a `malloc`-allocated pointer)."""
556	    if isinstance(param, ScalarParam):
557	        return param.name
558	    if isinstance(param, BufferParam):
559	        return f"&{param.name}" if _is_scalar_backed(param) else param.name
560	    raise HarnessError(f"unknown Param subtype: {type(param).__name__}")
561	
562	
563	def _is_scalar_backed(buf: BufferParam) -> bool:
564	    return buf.out and buf.length.strip() == "1"
565	
566	
567	def _strip_buffer_subscripts(expr: str, buffer_names: Collection[str]) -> str:
568	    """`expr` with every ``buf[...]`` subscript reduced to the bare buffer name.
569	
570	    Isolates the *index* uses of a buffer from the rest of the clause, so a caller
571	    can ask what a clause says about an identifier **outside** any subscript.
572	    One pattern per name rather than one alternation, so a name that prefixes
573	    another (`a` and `ab`) needs no ordering argument. Iterated to a fixpoint so a
574	    nested index (``a[b[0]]``) collapses inside-out: each substitution strictly
575	    shortens the text and an unbalanced ``[`` simply stops matching, so the loop
576	    always terminates -- with no buffers it settles after one no-op pass.
577	    """
578	    strippers = [
579	        re.compile(rf"\b({re.escape(name)})\s*\[[^\[\]]*\]") for name in buffer_names
580	    ]
581	    previous = ""
582	    while previous != expr:
583	        previous = expr
584	        for pattern in strippers:
585	            expr = pattern.sub(r"\1", expr)
586	    return expr
587	
588	
589	def _mixed_buffer_length_reason(
590	    preconditions: Sequence[str], buffers: Sequence[BufferParam]
591	) -> str | None:
592	    """Why a precondition cannot be ordered around its allocation, or None if all can.
593	
594	    A single clause that constrains *both* a buffer and the buffer's *size*
595	    (e.g. ``n >= 1 && n <= 2 && a[0] >= 0``) has no correct emission point: the
596	    length bound must precede the ``int *a = malloc(n * sizeof(int))``
597	    allocation, the buffer-content predicate must follow the nondet fill, and
598	    splitting arbitrary C on ``&&`` is unsound under ``||`` precedence.
599	
600	    Naming the length identifier is *not* itself a size constraint: in
601	    ``a[n - 1] >= 0`` the `n` is an index into an already-declared buffer, so the
602	    whole clause emits after the allocation and fill. Only a length identifier
603	    appearing **outside** a buffer subscript forces pre-allocation ordering, so
604	    the check strips ``a[...]`` (`_strip_buffer_subscripts`) before looking for
605	    one -- an index-use is renderable, an index-use combined with a genuine
606	    bound (``a[n - 1] >= 0 && n >= 1``) is still not.
607	
608	    This decides *emission ordering* only, never index bounds: whether ``n - 1``
609	    is in range for ``a[n]`` is ESBMC's to catch in the emitted harness, exactly as
610	    it already is for the long-accepted constant-index ``a[5] >= 0``.
611	
612	    Source-free -- it needs only the signature-derived buffers and the spec's
613	    preconditions -- so it is a `(signature, spec)` guard `renderability_reason`
614	    owns and `_split_assumptions` reuses: one rule, two callers, one message.
615	    """
616	    buffer_names = {buf.name for buf in buffers}
617	    length_idents = {ident for buf in buffers for ident in identifiers(buf.length)}
618	    for raw in preconditions:
619	        stripped = raw.strip()
620	        if not stripped or not any(references(stripped, n) for n in buffer_names):
621	            continue
622	        outside_indices = _strip_buffer_subscripts(stripped, buffer_names)
623	        if any(references(outside_indices, ident) for ident in length_idents):
624	            return (
625	                f"precondition {stripped!r} constrains both a buffer and a "
626	                "buffer-length identifier outside a subscript index; split it into "
627	                "separate domain entries so the length bound can precede the "
628	                "allocation it sizes"
629	            )
630	    return None
631	
632	
633	def _split_assumptions(
634	    preconditions: Sequence[str], buffers: Sequence[BufferParam]
635	) -> tuple[list[str], list[str]]:
636	    """Partition preconditions by whether they reference a buffer parameter.
637	
638	    A precondition over buffer *contents* (e.g. ``a[0] >= 0``, ``a[n - 1] >= 0``)
639	    can only be emitted once the buffer is declared and nondet-filled, so it goes
640	    *after* `_render_buffer` -- including when its index names the length, which by
641	    then is a bound scalar. A length/scalar-only precondition (e.g. ``len <= 4``)
642	    must stay *before* the allocation it sizes. Blank entries are dropped.
643	    Returns ``(pre_buffer, post_buffer)``.
644	
645	    A single clause constraining *both* a buffer and the buffer's size cannot be
646	    placed correctly; `_mixed_buffer_length_reason` -- the same guard
647	    `renderability_reason` consults statically -- names why, raised here as
648	    `HarnessError`. The caller supplies the length bound and the buffer predicate
649	    as separate `domain` entries instead. (In practice `render_semantic_harness`
650	    delegates to `renderability_reason` first, so this raise is the renderer's
651	    own invariant rather than the only line of defense.)
652	    """
653	    mixed = _mixed_buffer_length_reason(preconditions, buffers)
654	    if mixed is not None:
655	        raise HarnessError(mixed)
656	    buffer_names = {buf.name for buf in buffers}
657	    pre_buffer: list[str] = []
658	    post_buffer: list[str] = []
659	    for raw in preconditions:
660	        stripped = raw.strip()
661	        if not stripped:
662	            continue
663	        if any(references(stripped, name) for name in buffer_names):
664	            post_buffer.append(stripped)
665	        else:
666	            pre_buffer.append(stripped)
667	    return pre_buffer, post_buffer
668	
669	
670	def _defines_main(source: str) -> bool:
671	    """Whether `source` has a genuine, definition-shaped `main`.
672	
673	    Reuses `find_definition_brace` (comment-aware; requires a `{` body, not
674	    just the name) rather than a raw `\\bmain\\s*\\(` substring search — the
675	    latter also matches a bare comment mentioning `main`, which is not code
676	    at all (issue #95 review).
677	
678	    Deliberately narrower than "would this fail to compile": a *declaration*
679	    (prototype) is not itself a second definition the way this check cares
680	    about, but a signature mismatch between a left-behind prototype and the
681	    harness's own generated `int main(void) { ... }` is still a hard esbmc
682	    parse error ("conflicting types"), verified against a live esbmc run —
683	    this function alone does not catch that. Ensuring no `main`-named
684	    declaration of any signature reaches here is `Unit.from_path`'s job
685	    (`orchestrator/ports.py`'s `rename_all_declarations_and_definitions`; it
686	    renames a declaration alongside every definition), not this render-level
687	    guard's.
688	    """
689	    return find_definition_brace(source, "main") is not None

1	"""The typed C-signature model of a verification unit + a best-effort parser.
2	
3	A verification unit is keyed ``path::symbol`` (#62) but carries no types, so the
4	harness renderer needs the target symbol's C signature: its parameters, their
5	roles (scalar / input buffer / output buffer), and the return type. This module
6	owns that vocabulary (`ScalarParam`, `BufferParam`, `UnitSignature`) and the
7	regex parser (`extract_signature`) that recovers it from a unit's source text --
8	the concern `render_semantic_harness` (`harness.py`) deliberately keeps out of
9	the renderer so rendering stays fully testable without C parsing.
10	
11	The dependency is one-directional: ``harness`` imports from here, never the
12	reverse. `HarnessError` -- the fail-loud error shared by parsing and rendering --
13	therefore lives here (the parser raises it, `harness` re-imports it); a cycle is
14	the only alternative. No libclang/pycparser: the base install is dependency-free.
15	"""
16	
17	from __future__ import annotations
18	
19	import re
20	from collections.abc import Sequence
21	from dataclasses import dataclass
22	
23	
24	class HarnessError(ValueError):
25	    """The unit/property cannot be rendered into a valid harness (fail-loud)."""
26	
27	
28	@dataclass(frozen=True)
29	class ScalarParam:
30	    """A scalar arithmetic parameter, drawn from a single ``nondet_<T>()`` call."""
31	
32	    ctype: str  # type spelling as in the signature, e.g. "int64_t", "unsigned"
33	    name: str  # identifier the property references, e.g. "x"
34	
35	
36	@dataclass(frozen=True)
37	class BufferParam:
38	    """A pointer parameter backed by a nondet-filled (or output) heap buffer.
39	
40	    `length` is a C expression for the element count (usually another param's
41	    name, e.g. "len"); `out=True` means an output buffer -- allocated but NOT
42	    nondet-filled, referenced by `name` in the postcondition after the call. A
43	    single-element output (`length == "1"`) is backed by a scalar and passed by
44	    address (e.g. utf8's ``uint32_t *cp``); anything else is `malloc`-allocated,
45	    already a pointer at the call.
46	    """
47	
48	    elem_ctype: str  # e.g. "unsigned char", "int"
49	    name: str
50	    length: str
51	    const: bool = False
52	    out: bool = False
53	
54	
55	Param = ScalarParam | BufferParam  # sealed union (repo style)
56	
57	
58	@dataclass(frozen=True)
59	class UnitSignature:
60	    """The C signature of the unit ``path::symbol``.
61	
62	    The Property (#62) keys the unit as "path::symbol" but carries no types, so
63	    the signature is supplied here -- parsed by `extract_signature` or provided
64	    directly by the caller/proposer. `return_ctype` is "void" when the unit
65	    returns nothing.
66	    """
67	
68	    symbol: str
69	    return_ctype: str
70	    params: tuple[Param, ...]
71	
72	    @property
73	    def param_names(self) -> frozenset[str]:
74	        """Every parameter name, regardless of role."""
75	        return frozenset(p.name for p in self.params)
76	
77	    @property
78	    def output_param_names(self) -> frozenset[str]:
79	        """Names of the output parameters -- the `out=True` buffer params.
80	
81	        The unit *writes* these; the postcondition may name them after the call
82	        but a precondition may not constrain them (there is nothing there yet). A
83	        scalar-backed output (`length == "1"`) is an output like any other.
84	        """
85	        return frozenset(
86	            p.name for p in self.params if isinstance(p, BufferParam) and p.out
87	        )
88	
89	    @property
90	    def input_param_names(self) -> frozenset[str]:
91	        """Names of the input parameters -- every parameter that is not an output."""
92	        return self.param_names - self.output_param_names
93	
94	
95	_STORAGE_SPECIFIERS = frozenset({"static", "inline", "extern", "_Noreturn"})
96	_INT_TYPE_RE = re.compile(
97	    r"\b(?:unsigned|signed|int|short|long|char|_Bool|bool"
98	    r"|s?size_t|ptrdiff_t|u?int(?:_least|_fast)?\d+_t|u?intptr_t|u?intmax_t)\b"
99	)
100	_FLOAT_TYPE_RE = re.compile(r"\b(?:float|double)\b")
101	
102	
103	def extract_signature(unit_source: str, symbol: str) -> UnitSignature:
104	    """Best-effort regex parse of `symbol`'s signature from `unit_source`.
105	
106	    No libclang/pycparser (the base install is dependency-free). Isolated from
107	    `render_semantic_harness` so rendering stays fully testable without C
108	    parsing. Classifies a pointer param as a `BufferParam`, inferring its length
109	    from an immediately-following integer parameter (the ``(buf, len)`` idiom); a
110	    trailing non-const pointer is treated as a single-element output. Covers the
111	    corpus styles (abs, utf8_decode, murmur3_32); K&R decls and function-pointer
112	    params are out of scope. Raises `HarnessError` when the definition isn't
113	    found or a param can't be classified -- non-load-bearing and fail-loud, so a
114	    parser miss never silently corrupts a harness (the caller can always hand-
115	    build a `UnitSignature`).
116	    """
117	    pattern = re.compile(
118	        r"([A-Za-z_][\w \t\*]*?[\s\*])" + re.escape(symbol) + r"\s*\(([^)]*)\)\s*\{"
119	    )
120	    match = pattern.search(unit_source)
121	    if match is None:
122	        raise HarnessError(f"could not find a definition of {symbol!r} in unit_source")
123	    return_ctype = " ".join(
124	        t for t in match.group(1).split() if t not in _STORAGE_SPECIFIERS
125	    )
126	    if not return_ctype:
127	        raise HarnessError(f"could not parse the return type of {symbol!r}")
128	    raws = [_parse_fragment(frag, symbol) for frag in _split_params(match.group(2))]
129	    return UnitSignature(
130	        symbol=symbol,
131	        return_ctype=return_ctype,
132	        params=_to_params(raws),
133	    )
134	
135	
136	@dataclass(frozen=True)
137	class _RawParam:
138	    """A parameter fragment before buffer length/out inference."""
139	
140	    type_str: str
141	    name: str
142	    is_ptr: bool
143	    is_const: bool
144	    array_len: str | None
145	
146	
147	def _split_params(raw: str) -> list[str]:
148	    """Split a parameter list on top-level commas; ``""``/``void`` -> no params."""
149	    stripped = raw.strip()
150	    if stripped in ("", "void"):
151	        return []
152	    parts: list[str] = []
153	    depth = 0
154	    current: list[str] = []
155	    for ch in stripped:
156	        if ch in "([{":
157	            depth += 1
158	        elif ch in ")]}":
159	            depth -= 1
160	        if ch == "," and depth == 0:
161	            parts.append("".join(current))
162	            current = []
163	        else:
164	            current.append(ch)
165	    parts.append("".join(current))
166	    return [p.strip() for p in parts if p.strip()]
167	
168	
169	def _parse_fragment(frag: str, symbol: str) -> _RawParam:
170	    array = re.search(r"\[([^\]]*)\]", frag)
171	    array_len = (array.group(1).strip() or None) if array is not None else None
172	    body = (frag[: array.start()] + frag[array.end() :]) if array is not None else frag
173	    body = body.strip()
174	    name_match = re.search(r"([A-Za-z_]\w*)\s*$", body)
175	    if name_match is None:
176	        raise HarnessError(f"could not parse parameter {frag!r} of {symbol!r}")
177	    type_str = body[: name_match.start()].strip()
178	    if not type_str:
179	        raise HarnessError(f"could not parse the type of parameter {frag!r}")
180	    return _RawParam(
181	        type_str=type_str,
182	        name=name_match.group(1),
183	        is_ptr="*" in type_str or array is not None,
184	        is_const=bool(re.search(r"\bconst\b", type_str)),
185	        array_len=array_len,
186	    )
187	
188	
189	def _to_params(raws: Sequence[_RawParam]) -> tuple[Param, ...]:
190	    params: list[Param] = []
191	    for i, raw in enumerate(raws):
192	        if not raw.is_ptr:
193	            params.append(ScalarParam(ctype=raw.type_str, name=raw.name))
194	            continue
195	        nxt = raws[i + 1] if i + 1 < len(raws) else None
196	        if raw.array_len:
197	            length, out = raw.array_len, False
198	        elif nxt is not None and not nxt.is_ptr and _is_integer_type(nxt.type_str):
199	            length, out = nxt.name, False
200	        elif nxt is None:
201	            # a trailing pointer with no length param is a single-element output
202	            # (e.g. utf8_decode's `uint32_t *cp`); non-const -> written by the unit.
203	            length, out = "1", not raw.is_const
204	        else:
205	            # an interior pointer not followed by its integer length: ambiguous
206	            # (e.g. `dot(const int *a, const int *b, size_t n)`). Fail loud rather
207	            # than invent length 1 -- the caller hand-builds a UnitSignature for
208	            # multi-buffer signatures.
209	            raise HarnessError(
210	                f"cannot infer the length of pointer parameter {raw.name!r}: it is "
211	                "not the (buffer, length) idiom nor a trailing output; supply a "
212	                "UnitSignature explicitly for multi-buffer signatures"
213	            )
214	        params.append(
215	            BufferParam(
216	                elem_ctype=_elem_ctype(raw.type_str),
217	                name=raw.name,
218	                length=length,
219	                const=raw.is_const,
220	                out=out,
221	            )
222	        )
223	    return tuple(params)
224	
225	
226	def _elem_ctype(type_str: str) -> str:
227	    """A pointer/array param's element type: drop ``const`` and ``*``."""
228	    without_const = re.sub(r"\bconst\b", "", type_str).replace("*", " ")
229	    return " ".join(without_const.split())
230	
231	
232	def _is_integer_type(type_str: str) -> bool:
233	    return (
234	        _INT_TYPE_RE.search(type_str) is not None
235	        and _FLOAT_TYPE_RE.search(type_str) is None
236	    )
237

/* Recursive merge sort over a fixed-size int array. The kernel (msort/merge) is
 * portable C; main is the ESBMC harness. It sorts N nondet elements and asserts
 * the full correctness spec: the output is SORTED and is a PERMUTATION of the
 * input (multiset equality), so a degenerate "return a constant sorted array"
 * cannot pass.
 *
 * Two harness details are load-bearing for bounded model checking:
 *   - Element values are constrained to [0, 8) via __ESBMC_assume. The
 *     permutation check is O(N^2) over the values; with full-width nondet ints

"""Invoke ESBMC and classify its output into a typed `EsbmcResult`."""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
import re
import subprocess
import time
from collections.abc import Sequence
from pathlib import Path

from .cex_parser import Frontend, parse_counterexample
from .result import (
    Error,
    EsbmcResult,
    RunMeta,
    Unknown,
    UnknownReason,
    Verified,
    Violated,
)

_FAILED = "VERIFICATION FAILED"
_SUCCESSFUL = "VERIFICATION SUCCESSFUL"
_CEX_START = "[Counterexample]"
_RESULTS = "** Results:"


def _has_banner(text: str, banner: str) -> bool:
    """True only if `banner` appears as a standalone output line.

    ESBMC prints its verdict on its own line. Requiring a line match keeps a
    broken invocation that merely *echoes* the banner text (a frontend
    diagnostic quoting source, a preprocessor error) from being read as a
    verdict, per the "never silently pass" invariant.
    """
    return any(line.strip() == banner for line in text.splitlines())


def _counterexample(text: str) -> str:
    """The trace text spanning `[Counterexample]` up to the terminal FAILED banner.

    Slices at the *last* standalone FAILED line, not the first substring match —
    so a `VERIFICATION FAILED` echoed inside the `Violated property:` block (e.g.
    an `__ESBMC_assert` message) doesn't truncate the trace early. Also excludes
    the `** Results:` summary esbmc appends before that banner (new in 8.5): it
    lists every evaluated property's PASSED/FAILED/NOT CHECKED status, not just
    the one actually violated, so its text can contain "unwinding assertion" or
    a forseti obligation-site label for a check that never fired — callers that
    substring-search `raw_counterexample` (`precond.run._is_under_unwound`,
    `precond.reachability`, `precond.discharge`) would otherwise misread it.
    Callers only invoke this once a standalone FAILED banner is known to exist.
    """
    lines = text.splitlines()
    cut = len(lines)
    for i in range(len(lines) - 1, -1, -1):
        if lines[i].strip() == _FAILED:
            cut = i
            break
    for i in range(cut - 1, -1, -1):
        if lines[i] == _RESULTS:
            cut = i
            break
    body = "\n".join(lines[:cut])
    start = body.find(_CEX_START)
    return (body[start:] if start != -1 else body).strip()


def _error_message(text: str) -> str:
    """First `ERROR:`-prefixed line, so a known failure is self-describing."""
    for line in text.splitlines():
        if line.startswith("ERROR:"):
            return line[len("ERROR:") :].strip()
    return "esbmc reported an error"


def classify(meta: RunMeta, frontend: Frontend = Frontend.C) -> EsbmcResult:
    """Map one finished ESBMC run to a verdict.

    Classification keys on stdout/stderr markers, never the exit code (a
    timeout and a real violation both exit 1). Known invocation errors are
    checked before any verdict banner, and the SUCCESSFUL/FAILED banners are
    matched only as standalone lines — so a broken invocation that merely
    echoes banner text (a parse diagnostic quoting source) is never read as a
    verdict. Unrecognised output becomes `Error`, never a verdict. On VIOLATED
    the raw trace is parsed into a typed `Counterexample` for `frontend`;
    parsing returns `None` rather than disturbing the verdict on failure.
    """
    text = meta.stdout + "\n" + meta.stderr
    if (
        meta.exit_code == 6
        or "PARSING ERROR" in text
        or "failed to open input file" in text
    ):
        return Error(meta, _error_message(text))
    if _has_banner(text, _FAILED):
        raw = _counterexample(text)
        return Violated(meta, raw, parse_counterexample(raw, frontend))
    if _has_banner(text, _SUCCESSFUL):
        return Verified(meta)
    if "VERIFICATION UNKNOWN" in text:
        return Unknown(meta, UnknownReason.UNCLASSIFIED)
    if "Timed out" in text:
        return Unknown(meta, UnknownReason.TIMEOUT)
    if "Out of memory" in text:
        return Unknown(meta, UnknownReason.MEMOUT)
    return Error(meta, "unclassified output")


# Wall-clock slack added on top of esbmc's own --timeout before we hard-kill it.
# Public (not `_`-prefixed): a caller that sizes its OWN outer subprocess budget
# around one or more `verify` calls (e.g. the Claude Code adapter's property
# gate, which shells out to a `forseti check` subprocess running one `verify`
# per stored property) needs this same grace *per attempt* to avoid killing a
# child before it can emit output that already finished legitimately within
# esbmc's own `--timeout` (issue #95 review) -- a private module constant would
# force that caller to either reach into `runner`'s internals or hardcode a
# drifting duplicate.
VERIFY_GRACE_S = 5.0
_VERSION_RE = re.compile(r"ESBMC version (\S+)")


def _parse_version(text: str) -> str:
    match = _VERSION_RE.search(text)
    return match.group(1) if match else ""


def _as_text(value: str | bytes | None) -> str:
    """Captured subprocess output as text (decode bytes, treat None as empty)."""
    if value is None:
        return ""
    if isinstance(value, bytes):
        return value.decode("utf-8", "replace")
    return value


def _run_meta(
    argv: tuple[str, ...],
    *,
    exit_code: int,
    duration_s: float,
    stdout: str,
    stderr: str,
) -> RunMeta:
    """Assemble the provenance of one finished-or-failed esbmc invocation.

    The single place that turns a subprocess outcome into a `RunMeta`, so the
    version banner is parsed from the captured output the same way on every
    exit path. esbmc prints its banner before it starts solving, so a run that
    times out *after* the banner still records the build here — provenance the
    success-only version parse used to drop. When no banner was captured (the
    binary never ran, or the timeout fired first) `esbmc_version` stays empty.
    """
    return RunMeta(
        esbmc_version=_parse_version(stdout) or _parse_version(stderr),
        argv=argv,
        exit_code=exit_code,
        duration_s=duration_s,
        stdout=stdout,
        stderr=stderr,
    )


def _encode_timeout_s(timeout_s: float) -> str:
    """esbmc's `--timeout` value for a budget of `timeout_s` seconds.

    esbmc takes a whole-second count with a unit suffix. We round *up* to whole
    seconds and never below `1s`: a positive budget must stay a positive,
    bounded timeout. Plain truncation is the trap here — `int(0.5)` is `0`, and
    esbmc reads `--timeout 0s` as *no* timeout, silently turning a sub-second
    budget into an unbounded run. Rounding up also keeps esbmc's own timeout
    strictly under the wall-clock backstop (`timeout_s + VERIFY_GRACE_S`), so esbmc
    still self-terminates with a clean `Timed out` before we hard-kill it.
    """
    return f"{max(1, math.ceil(timeout_s))}s"


def build_argv(
    source: Path,
    *,
    unwind: int,
    function: str | None = None,
    timeout_s: float | None = None,
    extra_flags: Sequence[str] = (),
    esbmc_bin: str = "esbmc",
    no_unwinding_assertions: bool = True,
) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    """The exact esbmc command line for these verification parameters.

    The single home for every argv decision: the recommended
    `--unwind N --no-unwinding-assertions` bound, the optional `--function`
    entry point, the verbatim `extra_flags` passthrough, and the `--timeout`
    encoding. Keeping it pure and separate from the subprocess call makes the
    command line directly testable without invoking esbmc, and gives callers one
    place to spell a flag rather than open-coding `["--function", name]` at each
    site. `function` and `--timeout` come *after* `extra_flags` so an explicit
    passthrough flag keeps its position relative to esbmc's option precedence.

    `no_unwinding_assertions` defaults True (the corpus/gate bound: a VERIFIED is
    "up to k", an under-unwound loop is silently assumed exited). The memory-
    precondition synthesizer (RFC-0003 S2) sets it False so unwinding assertions
    are **on** — an under-unwound loop then reports a distinct *unwinding
    assertion* failure (the driver escalates k on it) rather than a fake proof.
    """
    argv = [
        esbmc_bin,
        str(source),
        "--unwind",
        str(unwind),
        *(("--no-unwinding-assertions",) if no_unwinding_assertions else ()),
        *extra_flags,
    ]
    if function is not None:
        argv += ["--function", function]
    if timeout_s is not None:
        argv += ["--timeout", _encode_timeout_s(timeout_s)]
    return tuple(argv)


def verify(
    source: Path,
    *,
    unwind: int,
    timeout_s: float | None = None,
    function: str | None = None,
    extra_flags: Sequence[str] = (),
    esbmc_bin: str = "esbmc",
    frontend: Frontend = Frontend.C,
    no_unwinding_assertions: bool = True,
) -> EsbmcResult:
    """Run ESBMC on a `source` and return the typed verdict.

    Uses the recommended `--unwind N --no-unwinding-assertions` bound. `unwind`
    is required and recorded in the result's `argv`, so a VERIFIED stays
    qualified as "verified up to k". `function` selects the entry point to
    verify (esbmc's `--function`), spelled as data here rather than by the
    caller. When `timeout_s` is set, esbmc's own `--timeout` is used (it yields a
    clean `Timed out`), with a wall-clock backstop that maps a Python-level
    timeout to `Unknown(TIMEOUT)`. `frontend` selects the counterexample parser
    (C only, for now). `no_unwinding_assertions` (default True) turns esbmc's
    unwinding assertions off; the S2 synthesizer passes False to keep them on.
    """
    argv = build_argv(
        source,
        unwind=unwind,
        function=function,
        timeout_s=timeout_s,
        extra_flags=extra_flags,
        esbmc_bin=esbmc_bin,
        no_unwinding_assertions=no_unwinding_assertions,
    )
    proc_timeout = timeout_s + VERIFY_GRACE_S if timeout_s is not None else None

    start = time.monotonic()
    try:
        proc = subprocess.run(
            argv, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=proc_timeout
        )
    except OSError as exc:
        # The binary never ran (missing, non-executable, a directory, ...);
        # record the intended argv for provenance. FileNotFoundError is an
        # OSError subclass, so a missing binary keeps its specific message;
        # PermissionError and other OSErrors become a typed Error too, never a
        # leaked exception, per the wrapper's "invocation failures are Error"
        # invariant.
        meta = _run_meta(
            argv,
            exit_code=-1,
            duration_s=time.monotonic() - start,
            stdout="",
            stderr="",
        )
        message = (
            f"esbmc binary not found: {esbmc_bin}"
            if isinstance(exc, FileNotFoundError)
            else f"esbmc invocation failed: {esbmc_bin}: {exc}"
        )
        return Error(meta, message)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as exc:
        meta = _run_meta(
            argv,
            exit_code=-1,
            duration_s=time.monotonic() - start,
            stdout=_as_text(exc.stdout),
            stderr=_as_text(exc.stderr),
        )
        return Unknown(meta, UnknownReason.TIMEOUT)

    meta = _run_meta(
        argv,
        exit_code=proc.returncode,
        duration_s=time.monotonic() - start,
        stdout=proc.stdout,
        stderr=proc.stderr,
    )
    return classify(meta, frontend)

"""Typed model of an ESBMC counterexample.

ESBMC emits no proof object. When it returns the VIOLATED verdict it prints a
concrete *counterexample*: an ordered trace of program states (the path) ending
in the property that was violated. This module is the typed, faithful model of
that trace — the frontend-aware parsing of ESBMC's text into it lives in
`cex_parser`.

Fields are restricted to `str | int | None | tuple` so the whole structure
serializes cleanly (see `Counterexample.to_dict`) for the observability JSONL
trace and the result cache.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass
from typing import Any

_BASE_SYMBOL_RE = re.compile(r"^[^$\[.]+")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SourceLoc:
    """A source location as ESBMC prints it; `function` is absent on some states."""

    file: str
    line: int
    column: int
    function: str | None


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Assignment:
    """One `lhs = value` binding in a trace step.

    `value` is ESBMC's raw right-hand side (e.g. `-2147483648`, `(signed int *)0`,
    `ARRAY_OF(0)`); `binary` is the trailing bit-string ESBMC shows for scalars,
    or `None` when none was printed.
    """

    lhs: str
    value: str
    binary: str | None


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Step:
    """One ESBMC trace state: its source location and the assignments made there.

    `number` is the state number exactly as printed — ESBMC's slicer drops
    states, so these are not contiguous and must not be re-indexed.
    """

    number: int
    loc: SourceLoc
    assignments: tuple[Assignment, ...]


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ViolatedProperty:
    """The property ESBMC found violated at the end of the path."""

    loc: SourceLoc
    description: str
    expression: str | None
    cwe: tuple[str, ...]


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Counterexample:
    """A parsed ESBMC counterexample: the ordered path plus the violated property."""

    steps: tuple[Step, ...]
    violated_property: ViolatedProperty

    @property
    def inputs(self) -> tuple[Assignment, ...]:
        """The first assignment seen for each distinct base variable.

        A *heuristic* "concrete input seeds" view: ESBMC's trace doesn't mark
        which assignments are nondet inputs versus computed values, so this
        keeps the earliest write per base source symbol (SSA suffix `$...` and
        any `[index]`/`.field` accessor stripped). The faithful, complete path
        lives in `steps`.
        """
        seen: set[str] = set()
        out: list[Assignment] = []
        for step in self.steps:
            for assignment in step.assignments:
                match = _BASE_SYMBOL_RE.match(assignment.lhs)
                base = match.group(0) if match else assignment.lhs
                if base not in seen:
                    seen.add(base)
                    out.append(assignment)
        return tuple(out)

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """A JSON-serializable dict (for the observability trace / result cache).

        Every field is `str | int | None | tuple`, so `asdict` yields a structure
        `json.dumps` accepts directly. The `inputs` view is derived, not stored.
        """
        return asdict(self)
"""Frontend-aware parser: ESBMC counterexample text -> typed `Counterexample`.

Only the C frontend is implemented (ADR-0003: C first, then C++, then Python);
`Frontend` is the extension point so later frontends slot in without touching
callers. `parse_counterexample` never raises and returns `None` on any failure,
so attaching a parsed model can never downgrade or break the VIOLATED verdict.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from enum import Enum

from .counterexample import (
    Assignment,
    Counterexample,
    SourceLoc,
    Step,
    ViolatedProperty,
)


class Frontend(Enum):
    """ESBMC source frontend a counterexample came from (C only, for now)."""

    C = "c"


_STATE_RE = re.compile(
    r"^State (\d+) file (.+?) line (\d+) column (\d+)"
    r"(?: function (.+?))? thread (\d+)$"
)
_LOC_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*file (.+?) line (\d+) column (\d+)(?: function (.+?))?$")
_VIOLATED = "Violated property:"
_CEX_MARKER = "[Counterexample]"
_BINARY_RE = re.compile(r"\s+\(([01]+(?: [01]+)*)\)$")


def _loc(file: str, line: str, column: str, function: str | None) -> SourceLoc:
    return SourceLoc(
        file=file, line=int(line), column=int(column), function=function or None
    )


def _assignment(body: str) -> Assignment:
    """Parse one `lhs = value` line, peeling ESBMC's trailing bit-string if shown."""
    lhs, _, rhs = body.partition(" = ")
    rhs = rhs.strip()
    binary: str | None = None
    match = _BINARY_RE.search(rhs)
    if match:
        binary = match.group(1)
        rhs = rhs[: match.start()].rstrip()
    return Assignment(lhs=lhs.strip(), value=rhs, binary=binary)


def _opens_block(line: str) -> bool:
    """A `State` header or the `Violated property:` line ends the current block."""
    return bool(_STATE_RE.match(line.strip())) or line.startswith(_VIOLATED)


def _parse_state(lines: list[str], i: int) -> tuple[Step, int]:
    """Parse a `State` block starting at line `i`; return the Step and next index."""
    m = _STATE_RE.match(lines[i].strip())
    number, file, ln, col, fn, _thread = m.groups()  # ty: ignore[unresolved-attribute]
    assignments: list[Assignment] = []
    i += 1
    while i < len(lines) and not _opens_block(lines[i]):
        body = lines[i].strip()
        if body and set(body) != {"-"} and " = " in body:
            assignments.append(_assignment(body))
        i += 1
    step = Step(int(number), _loc(file, ln, col, fn), tuple(assignments))
    return step, i


def _parse_violated(lines: list[str], i: int) -> tuple[ViolatedProperty | None, int]:
    """Parse a `Violated property:` block → the property (or None) and next index.

    Layout: a `file … line … column … function …` location line, then a human
    description, optional `CWE: <id>[, <id>…]` line(s), and an optional trailing
    violated expression (absent for e.g. a NULL-pointer dereference).
    """
    i += 1
    loc_match = _LOC_RE.match(lines[i]) if i < len(lines) else None
    if loc_match is None:
        return None, i
    file, ln, col, fn = loc_match.groups()
    i += 1
    cwe: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    detail: list[str] = []
    while i < len(lines) and lines[i][:1] in (" ", "\t"):
        text = lines[i].strip()

"""Typed model of an ESBMC counterexample.

ESBMC emits no proof object. When it returns the VIOLATED verdict it prints a
concrete *counterexample*: an ordered trace of program states (the path) ending
in the property that was violated. This module is the typed, faithful model of
that trace — the frontend-aware parsing of ESBMC's text into it lives in
`cex_parser`.

Fields are restricted to `str | int | None | tuple` so the whole structure
serializes cleanly (see `Counterexample.to_dict`) for the observability JSONL
trace and the result cache.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass
from typing import Any

_BASE_SYMBOL_RE = re.compile(r"^[^$\[.]+")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SourceLoc:
    """A source location as ESBMC prints it; `function` is absent on some states."""

    file: str
    line: int
    column: int
    function: str | None


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Assignment:
    """One `lhs = value` binding in a trace step.

    `value` is ESBMC's raw right-hand side (e.g. `-2147483648`, `(signed int *)0`,
    `ARRAY_OF(0)`); `binary` is the trailing bit-string ESBMC shows for scalars,
    or `None` when none was printed.
    """

    lhs: str
    value: str
    binary: str | None


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Step:
    """One ESBMC trace state: its source location and the assignments made there.

    `number` is the state number exactly as printed — ESBMC's slicer drops
    states, so these are not contiguous and must not be re-indexed.
    """

    number: int
    loc: SourceLoc
    assignments: tuple[Assignment, ...]


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ViolatedProperty:
    """The property ESBMC found violated at the end of the path."""

    loc: SourceLoc
    description: str
    expression: str | None
    cwe: tuple[str, ...]


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Counterexample:
    """A parsed ESBMC counterexample: the ordered path plus the violated property."""

    steps: tuple[Step, ...]
    violated_property: ViolatedProperty

    @property
    def inputs(self) -> tuple[Assignment, ...]:
        """The first assignment seen for each distinct base variable.

        A *heuristic* "concrete input seeds" view: ESBMC's trace doesn't mark
        which assignments are nondet inputs versus computed values, so this
        keeps the earliest write per base source symbol (SSA suffix `$...` and
        any `[index]`/`.field` accessor stripped). The faithful, complete path
        lives in `steps`.
        """
        seen: set[str] = set()
        out: list[Assignment] = []
        for step in self.steps:
            for assignment in step.assignments:
                match = _BASE_SYMBOL_RE.match(assignment.lhs)
                base = match.group(0) if match else assignment.lhs
                if base not in seen:
                    seen.add(base)
                    out.append(assignment)
        return tuple(out)

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """A JSON-serializable dict (for the observability trace / result cache).

        Every field is `str | int | None | tuple`, so `asdict` yields a structure
        `json.dumps` accepts directly. The `inputs` view is derived, not stored.
        """
        return asdict(self)
"""Frontend-aware parser: ESBMC counterexample text -> typed `Counterexample`.

Only the C frontend is implemented (ADR-0003: C first, then C++, then Python);
`Frontend` is the extension point so later frontends slot in without touching
callers. `parse_counterexample` never raises and returns `None` on any failure,
so attaching a parsed model can never downgrade or break the VIOLATED verdict.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from enum import Enum

from .counterexample import (
    Assignment,
    Counterexample,
    SourceLoc,
    Step,
    ViolatedProperty,
)


class Frontend(Enum):
    """ESBMC source frontend a counterexample came from (C only, for now)."""

    C = "c"


_STATE_RE = re.compile(
    r"^State (\d+) file (.+?) line (\d+) column (\d+)"
    r"(?: function (.+?))? thread (\d+)$"
)
_LOC_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*file (.+?) line (\d+) column (\d+)(?: function (.+?))?$")
_VIOLATED = "Violated property:"
_CEX_MARKER = "[Counterexample]"
_BINARY_RE = re.compile(r"\s+\(([01]+(?: [01]+)*)\)$")


def _loc(file: str, line: str, column: str, function: str | None) -> SourceLoc:
    return SourceLoc(
        file=file, line=int(line), column=int(column), function=function or None
    )


def _assignment(body: str) -> Assignment:
    """Parse one `lhs = value` line, peeling ESBMC's trailing bit-string if shown."""
    lhs, _, rhs = body.partition(" = ")
    rhs = rhs.strip()
    binary: str | None = None
    match = _BINARY_RE.search(rhs)
    if match:
        binary = match.group(1)
        rhs = rhs[: match.start()].rstrip()
    return Assignment(lhs=lhs.strip(), value=rhs, binary=binary)


def _opens_block(line: str) -> bool:
    """A `State` header or the `Violated property:` line ends the current block."""
    return bool(_STATE_RE.match(line.strip())) or line.startswith(_VIOLATED)


def _parse_state(lines: list[str], i: int) -> tuple[Step, int]:
    """Parse a `State` block starting at line `i`; return the Step and next index."""
    m = _STATE_RE.match(lines[i].strip())
    number, file, ln, col, fn, _thread = m.groups()  # ty: ignore[unresolved-attribute]
    assignments: list[Assignment] = []
    i += 1
    while i < len(lines) and not _opens_block(lines[i]):
        body = lines[i].strip()
        if body and set(body) != {"-"} and " = " in body:
            assignments.append(_assignment(body))
        i += 1
    step = Step(int(number), _loc(file, ln, col, fn), tuple(assignments))
    return step, i


def _parse_violated(lines: list[str], i: int) -> tuple[ViolatedProperty | None, int]:
    """Parse a `Violated property:` block → the property (or None) and next index.

    Layout: a `file … line … column … function …` location line, then a human
    description, optional `CWE: <id>[, <id>…]` line(s), and an optional trailing
    violated expression (absent for e.g. a NULL-pointer dereference).
    """
    i += 1
    loc_match = _LOC_RE.match(lines[i]) if i < len(lines) else None
    if loc_match is None:
        return None, i
    file, ln, col, fn = loc_match.groups()
    i += 1
    cwe: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    detail: list[str] = []
    while i < len(lines) and lines[i][:1] in (" ", "\t"):
        text = lines[i].strip()
        if text.startswith("CWE:"):
            cwe = tuple(p.strip() for p in text[len("CWE:") :].split(",") if p.strip())
        elif text:
            detail.append(text)
        i += 1
    prop = ViolatedProperty(
        loc=_loc(file, ln, col, fn),
        description=detail[0] if detail else "",
        expression=detail[1] if len(detail) > 1 else None,
        cwe=cwe,
    )
    return prop, i


def _parse_c(raw: str) -> Counterexample | None:
    lines = raw.splitlines()
    # Some flag combinations (e.g. --assertion-coverage) emit several
    # [Counterexample] blocks, each for a different violated property, before one
    # terminal banner. Merging their states under a single property would be a
    # synthetic trace mixing assertions — decline rather than mislead (the caller
    # keeps the lossless raw_counterexample).
    if sum(1 for line in lines if line.strip() == _CEX_MARKER) > 1:
        return None
    steps: list[Step] = []
    prop: ViolatedProperty | None = None
    i = 0
    while i < len(lines):
        if _STATE_RE.match(lines[i].strip()):
            step, i = _parse_state(lines, i)
            steps.append(step)
        elif lines[i].startswith(_VIOLATED):
            prop, i = _parse_violated(lines, i)
        else:
            i += 1

    if prop is None:
        return None
    return Counterexample(steps=tuple(steps), violated_property=prop)


def parse_counterexample(
    raw: str, frontend: Frontend = Frontend.C
) -> Counterexample | None:
    """Parse ESBMC counterexample text into a typed model, or `None` on failure.

    Returns `None` (never raises) when the text can't be parsed, so the caller's
    VIOLATED verdict and `raw_counterexample` fallback are always preserved.
    """
    try:
        if frontend is Frontend.C:
            return _parse_c(raw)
    except Exception:
        return None
    return None
